annotation.method: Codex freshly read the complete 21-page PDF in physical order, including Sections 1-8, all algorithms and recurrence formulas, all numerical figures and observations, Appendix A, and all references, then compared every source-proved candidate with Mathlib and the frozen importable NumStability baseline.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P42 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

corpus_membership: This paper is part of the current corpus listed in metadata/manifest.json.
paper_version: technical report SOL 2010-2, version of August 16, 2011, revised March 14, 2011

rejected_candidates.candidate: LSMR equivalence to MINRES applied to the normal equations
rejected_candidates.reason: The paper presents the equivalence through the known MINRES framework rather than supplying a new self-contained convergence theorem that maps to a qualifying compiled NumStability result.
The normal-equation kernel identity is proved in one line and is too easy for any tier.

The minimum-norm conclusion is source-proved but materially shorter and less technically demanding than Appendix A. It has no compiled NumStability shortcut and is not strong enough to replace the selected T3 candidate.
The quotient comparison follows immediately from the displayed backward-error definitions and is too easy for any tier.
The formulas and optimal backward-error characterization are attributed to earlier work rather than proved as new results in this paper.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Algorithms, stopping rules, and numerical experiments
rejected_candidates.reason: These specify computations or report empirical behavior rather than additional source-proved universal results suitable for a formal proof task.

T1.decision: Skipped. No complete source-proved result needs exactly one substantial theorem from the frozen compiled NumStability surface. Generic Givens and QR declarations do not replace the coupled LSMR recurrence argument.

T2.decision: Skipped. No complete source-proved result receives two distinct substantial compiled-library shortcuts. Treating generic rotation facts as two results would not discharge Appendix A and would create an artificial decomposition.

T3.decision: Selected the full scalar-recurrence form of Lemma 3.1. Appendix A supplies a multi-page arbitrary-index proof through three rotations, product identity (A.7), and the final induction; neither Mathlib nor NumStability provides a corresponding shortcut.

selection_policy: Use only conclusions whose statements and supporting proofs appear in this paper.
Do not turn standard MINRES, LSQR, or Golub-Kahan results cited from earlier work into P42 tasks.
Do not promote the one-line kernel lemma or quotient comparison to a benchmark tier.
Do not count generic Givens or QR infrastructure as a substantial NumStability result for the paper-specific coupled recurrence.
Retain Lemma 3.1 only in its arbitrary-iteration form and without assuming product identity (A.7) or the mixed-rotation cancellation.
Assign a tier only after exact private N and L proofs compile.
